prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universal “best” lawyer — the right personal-injury attorney for a Houston car wreck depends on facts of your case and what you value (trial experience, injury severity, track record, communication style, fee structure, etc.). I can help you find a strong match. To get started, here’s a practical plan and what to look for.

How to choose the right lawyer
- Experience with car-wreck cases like yours: look for attorneys who focus on vehicle collisions and catastrophic injury (not a generalist).
- Trial experience and verdicts: firms that will take cases to trial if insurers lowball are often stronger negotiators.
- Track record and settlements/verdicts: past results for cases similar in severity.
- Reputation and peer ratings: Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Avvo, Google/Yelp reviews.
- Communication and availability: responsiveness and a clear point of contact.
- Fee arrangement: most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover), so ask their percentage and how costs are handled.
- Compatibility and trust: you’ll work closely with them—trust matters.

Where to search
- State Bar of Texas lawyer referral and directories
- SuperLawyers.com (Texas/Houston lists)
- Martindale-Hubbell peer-review ratings
- Avvo (client reviews and ratings)
- Local Google/Yelp reviews and the firm’s website (look for case results)

What to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-crash cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? What were the outcomes?
- Who in the firm will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee (contingency %)? Who pays expenses if we don’t win?
- Do you accept cases that require medical liens? How are medical bills handled?
- What is your estimated timeline and likely range of recovery?
- Can you provide references from former clients?

Documents to bring to a consultation
- Police report
- Photos of vehicles, scene, injuries
- Medical records and bills (or list of providers)
- Insurance information (yours and other driver’s)
- Correspondence with insurers
- Names/contact info of witnesses

Important legal notes
- Texas statute of limitations: generally 2 years from the crash date to file a personal-injury lawsuit (there are exceptions). Act promptly.
- Don’t sign releases or give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without consulting an attorney.
- Seek medical care right away and document your injuries.

If you’d like, I can:
- Help you find top-rated Houston personal-injury attorneys (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood and any priorities: trial experience, bilingual, large firm vs boutique, severe injury vs minor).
- Draft a message or list of questions to send to lawyers when you contact them.

Which would you prefer?
